clue.text: Capital advises by radio on hospital administrators locally

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece 'on' another comes after it, so the radio word follows the hospital letter

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: something heard by radio is only heard, so the word for 'advises' is taken by its sound

parts.note: counsels means advises

explanation.surface: A capital city's broadcast advice about hospital managers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by radio' says COUNSELS is heard, giving COUNCILS; 'on' puts that after H in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Parish councils are the lowest tier of English local government, running village affairs.

clue.text: Disciplines studied by dancing star?

parts.note: a dancing star trains in dance, drama and music; and cryptically, the second word read as letters 'performing' gives star

explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic hint lies in the answer itself: ARTS, rearranged ('performing'), gives STAR, so 'dancing star' points at the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance, drama and music are the stage disciplines a stage star learns, collectively called this.

clue.text: Strained, being annoyed about demand after vacation

indicators.note: the word for annoyed goes round, or about, the remaining letters

parts.note: riled means annoyed

indicators.note: a word after vacation has been emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone tense and irritated by a request made just after returning from holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strained' reads as tense, but means passed through a sieve. 'after vacation' empties a word to its outer letters; 'about' wraps the annoyed word round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle is to pass through a coarse sieve, so riddled soil has been sieved or strained.

clue.text: Clear line adopted by agitated vets in feed

indicators.note: a thing adopted is taken in, so the line letter is taken into the jumbled letters
agitated letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: An obvious line taken by anxious vets over animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' scrambles VETS IN FEED, and 'adopted by' places L inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth needs no proof because it is plain or obvious on its face.

clue.text: Charlie may turn up for drink

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up reverses the words for may and turn

parts.note: can means may, as in having permission
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie might arrive at a bar for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses CANGO to OGNAC, written after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a brandy from the Cognac region of France, a spirit served as an after-dinner tipple.

clue.text: United — sending off anonymously

definitions.note: the clue's adverb stands for the adjective, as in a letter sent unsigned

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: off signals that the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Manchester United player is sent off, without anyone being named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal, not part of a red card. The adverb definition fits loosely: a note sent unsigned is sent anonymously.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsigned carries no name, so its author is unknown, exactly as with an anonymous letter.

clue.text: My bill!

definitions.meaning: ...! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'
doves bill and ..., so to ... is what lovebirds do while they bill

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a surprised exclamation at a restaurant bill, but it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo is an old-fashioned British exclamation of amazement, and also the soft murmur of doves billing.

clue.text: Child's toy muffling bird song

indicators.note: to muffle something is to wrap it up, so the toy wraps round the bird

parts.note: Lego is a children's building-brick toy
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A child's plaything drowning out the singing of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muffling' is the container signal; 'song' is the definition, not the bird's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Let It Go is the hit number from Disney's film Frozen, a song children know well.

clue.text: Poor toddler who ate last of food must be asleep

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the word food
poor here means badly formed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unwell toddler who has eaten the remains of dinner will soon be fast asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' scrambles TODDLER WHO ATE plus D, the 'last of' food.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dead to the world is so deeply asleep that nothing around them registers.

clue.text: China's standard warning?

definitions.meaning: a standard is a flag, and the national flag of China is red

explanation.definitionFit: China's flag is red, and a red flag is the classic signal of danger ahead.

clue.text: Dog bed in its new home at last

indicators.note: the bed is placed inside the rearranged letters
new signals the letters of its are made over in a fresh order

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word home

explanation.surface: A dog finally gets its bed in its new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' scrambles the word its to STI, 'in' sets the bed inside, and 'at last' supplies the final letter of home.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is a Scottish terrier, a short-legged wiry-coated breed.

clue.text: Blended contents of solid fuel

indicators.note: blended letters are mixed together into a new order
the contents of a word are its inner letters, without the ends

explanation.surface: A mix of the components of a solid fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of' solid gives OLI, which 'Blended' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is burned for heat and power, as in heating oil or diesel.

clue.text: Overdramatised and had daughter by former Rolling Stone (not Jack)

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: not removes the following letter from the Stone's name

parts.note: Mick Jagger is the Rolling Stones' singer
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards
ate means had, as in had a meal

explanation.surface: An ex-Rolling Stone's family drama, overplayed in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Mick Jagger is the singer meant; 'not Jack' strips the card abbreviation from his surname, and 'by' simply sets pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate is to overstate, so something exaggerated has been overdone or made more dramatic.

clue.text: Guideline set by Tom when in charge?

definitions.text: set by Tom when in charge?
definitions.meaning: Tom Thumb, the tiny folk hero

explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized hero of an English fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule of thumb is an approximate working principle drawn from experience rather than strict theory.

clue.text: Note milk supplier cut flying

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a dairy supplies milk

explanation.surface: A memo that the milkman's delivery has been stopped, sent by air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the milk supplier; 'flying' is the definition, in the sense of airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-air means up in the sky, off the ground, the position of something in flight.

clue.text: Affluent provider of 11 to act

parts.note: 11 across is oil, and an oil well supplies it
to do is to act

explanation.surface: A wealthy oil baron who supplies fuel decides to take action.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 11 means OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do people are prosperous, comfortably off with plenty of money.

clue.text: Uplifting spread allowed such a communication

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting up reverses the order of the letters

parts.note: marge, short for margarine, is a spread
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Cheering news about margarine being permitted, sent by wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' reverses MARGELET. 'such a' nods to this newspaper's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by telegraph, which is the name of this puzzle's paper.

clue.text: Insensitive? I'm not sure editor counted

parts.note: numb means without feeling
er is the hesitant sound of someone unsure

explanation.surface: An unfeeling editor hesitantly admits to having totted something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbered pages or days have been counted off or given numbers in sequence.

clue.text: Giant insect covering a couple of metres

indicators.note: the insect wraps round, or covers, the other letters

parts.note: a moth is an insect
M is the abbreviation for metre, so two metres give two Ms

explanation.surface: An enormous bug spanning two metres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' has the insect split open after its first letter to hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth, from the huge extinct elephant, means enormous; as a noun it names a giant creature.

clue.text: Cleaner, Flash, regularly put on lavatory

indicators.note: in an across entry, put on means placed after

parts.note: loo is British slang for lavatory

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word Flash

explanation.surface: Flash is a British cleaning brand, here applied to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes FAH from Flash, which is 'put on' LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried gourd sponge used for scrubbing the skin in the bath.

clue.text: Attitude underpinning footballers' wily ploy

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece underpinning another sits beneath it

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, the body of English football, so footballers' gives FA's
tone means attitude, as in the tone of a remark

explanation.surface: A mindset that supports the cunning tactic of a football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underpinning' puts TONE below FAS. The FA is England's Football Association.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a fast one is to play a crafty trick on someone.

clue.text: Short sharp tug, and snake gets a rodent

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a jerk is a sudden sharp pull
a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A quick pull on a snake catches a small animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks JERK to JER, followed by BOA.
explanation.definitionFit: The jerboa is a small jumping desert rodent with long hind legs.

clue.text: Concede maid works best after time

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the time letter
works here means is worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to best is to defeat

explanation.surface: A housemaid's labours prove best once time is up, someone admits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' is the anagram signal on maid, giving ADMI; 'after' places the word for best behind the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit defeat is to accept you have lost, to give in or concede.

clue.text: There's no end of nosh in spectacular spread

indicators.note: no means without, so the chosen letter is removed

parts.note: a spectacular is a lavish show

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word nosh

explanation.surface: A buffet looks grand, but all the food has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of nosh' removes H, the last letter of nosh, from SHOW. 'spread' looks like the buffet, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sow seed is to scatter or spread it across the ground.

clue.text: Nothing in rejected account is private

indicators.note: the letter for nothing goes inside the turned account
rejected means sent back, so the word for account is read backwards

parts.note: a report is an account of events
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A spurned story contained nothing, which is a personal matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns REPORT into TROPER; 'in' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier in a cavalry or armoured regiment, the lowest rank.

clue.text: Wash up for bestie, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down entry, up reverses the letters

parts.note: waves lap or wash against the shore

explanation.surface: Doing the dishes for a best friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash up' looks like doing dishes, but 'up' reverses LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestie is a best friend, one example of a pal or mate.

clue.text: Bishop and Brazilian couple going back for room

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: going back reverses the order of the letters

parts.note: Rio, short for Rio de Janeiro, is a Brazilian city
a duo is a couple

explanation.surface: A bishop and two Brazilians head back to their room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' reverses RIODUO to OUDOIR, after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A boudoir is a woman's private sitting room or bedroom.

clue.text: All home-brewed — a new product from the baker

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Everything is made at home, including a new loaf from the bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ALL HOME BREWED and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal bread is a loaf made from whole-grain flour, a staple sold in bakeries.
